title: Sapphire lawgiving, jasper, and the Scythian ravine hyacinth
english: smeared on the ulcerated places with milk. And the giving of the law on the mountain to Moses is said to have appeared on a sapphire stone. Iaspis is greenish, and it is found at the mouth of the river Mermodon and near Amathus in Cyprus. It is useful for epileptic seizures. Hyacinth is somewhat fiery-red, and it is found in inner Scythia, the barbarian land. The ancients used to call the whole northern region Scythia, where the Goths and Danes are. There, deep within the desert of great Scythia, is a ravine of immense depth, inaccessible to human beings, walled in on both sides by crags of rock, so that if someone leans over from the top of the mountains, as from a wall, he cannot see the floor of the ravine, but from its depth it is darkened like a chaos. In this ravine are condemned men sent by the kings who live nearby, and they are forced to work there. They slaughter lambs, skin them, and throw them down from the rocks above into the chaos of the ravine, and the stones stick to that meat. Then eagles that live on the rocks above come down at the smell of the meat and carry up the lambs with the stones. But while they eat the meat, the stones remain on the summit of the mountains.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Epiphanius continues his catalogue of the twelve stones, moving from the sapphire's healing use to the lawgiving on a sapphire stone, then to jasper and the legendary Scythian ravine where the hyacinth is found.

title: The condemned men retrieve the stones; properties of hyacinth, agate, amethyst, chrysolite, beryl, onyx
english: The condemned men observe where the eagles carried the meat, go there, and so bring back the stones. The stones have this power: when thrown onto burning coals, they are not harmed, and they quench the coals.

And not only this, but if someone takes the stone, wraps it in a linen cloth, and places it on the coals, while he holds it, he himself is scorched by the fire, yet the linen cloth remains unharmed. It is also said to help women in labor for the sake of easy delivery.
The agate is somewhat dark blue, and it too is found in those regions of Scythia. When rubbed on the forehead, it turns away the pain of a bite from scorpions and vipers.

The amethyst is deeply fiery, and it is found in the mountains of Libya near the shores of the sea. The chrysolite is golden, and it is found in the Aphraitis rock, beside the edge of Achemenid Babylon. For they call Babylon and that well of the rock Achemenis. When rubbed, it serves as medicine for those with stomach ailments, for those with colic, and for those with intestinal ailments.
The beryl is bluish-gray, and it occurs near the foothills of the mountain called Taurus. The onyx is yellow, and it too is found on the same mountain.
From Epiphanius, from the work addressed to Diodorus.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Epiphanius continues describing how the condemned men retrieve the hyacinth stones from the ravine, then lists the powers and places of origin of several stones on the breastplate.

title: Why Samaritans keep the law yet worship idols
english: The mountain was called Mount Somoron, and so were the neighboring regions, after Shemir, one of the sons of the Canaanites, before Abraham ever set foot in the land. When the guards arrived, they were called Samaritans, which means guards. They were guards not only of the land but also of the law, for they kept the Pentateuch alone, which they had received through Ezra the king, so that the seed of Abraham might be marked out by this. Yet they did not keep the law fully, and so Scripture says, "They went on keeping the law of God, yet worshiping the idols" (2 Kings 17:32-33).

Since the law commands that idols are not to be worshiped, how can this saying still be fulfilled? The explanation runs in this way. When the priests of the four nations learned that Ezra had settled here, since he abhors idols according to the law of God, they hastened to hide the idols in a recess on Mount Garizim, and they turned the hearts of the Samaritans to pray toward the mountain.

So wherever they are, they pray toward the mountain: those from the east turning away toward the west, those from the west toward the east, and those from the north toward the south, and [those from the south] toward the north, fixing their attention on the mountain as they pray, so that Scripture may be fulfilled which says, "They went on keeping the law of God, yet worshiping their own idols" (2 Kings 17:32-33). For even if they themselves do not know that the idols lie there, divine Scripture cannot lie.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Epiphanius finishes by explaining where the Samaritans came from and how their prayer toward Mount Garizim fulfills Scripture.
